subject: Post-call: Air-gapped fit assessment & scope confirmation
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Li Cheng <li.cheng@novagenomics.com>, Amanda Ruiz <amanda.ruiz@biometa.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Air-gapped fit assessment & scope confirmation

Hi Li / Amanda —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can converge on whether Private (air-gapped on-prem) is the right path vs Dedicated reservation: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Workload: batch inference for genomic variant scoring, variable peak QPS ~150 requests/min, median payload ~450 tokens, 90th percentile request spikes tied to nightly processing windows.
- Data residency & control: must remain in physically isolated network — no egress to public internet; on-site KV cache and model artifacts only.
- Upgrade cadence: target quarterly model updates with a planned maintenance window; customer requires deterministic offline upgrade MOP and rollback story.
- Availability: can tolerate short planned outages during maintenance, but need documented fallback to a reduced-capacity local model during critical processing.
- Procurement: site will provision standard 4U rack space, separate admin VLAN, and an airgap jump host for out-of-band support.

What we'll deliver next (internal & external):
1) Hardware profile recommendation tailored to your throughput and peak runbook (attached: onprem-hw-profile.pdf).
2) Draft maintenance and offline upgrade MOP for review (attached: mop-draft.docx).
3) Sizing options comparing Private air-gapped vs Dedicated capacity (cost delta + SLAs).
4) Suggested acceptance test matrix for on-site validation.

As immediate asks from you: 
- Confirm expected sustained tokens/day and whether nightly job windows are fixed (start/end times).
- Confirm whether physical access for our field engineer is available for acceptance testing, and any site constraints (visitor/clearance).

Next steps: If you agree, Ben will schedule a short technical call with your infra lead to validate power/cooling and remote console constraints. We can target a draft PSA and procurement checklist by next Wed (2026-08-05).

Thanks — I looped in Ben and Priyom for procurement and ops input.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai]
[attachment: onprem-hw-profile.pdf]
From: Li Cheng <li.cheng@novagenomics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amanda Ruiz <amanda.ruiz@biometa.io>
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 08:42:00 +0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Air-gapped fit assessment & scope confirmation

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Sustained load: our everyday throughput is lower (~40 req/min), but we have two nightly batch windows (01:00–03:00 and 22:00–23:30 SGT) where we expect the 150 req/min spikes. We also run ad-hoc large reanalysis jobs once every 2–3 weeks.

2) Physical access: we have a visitor clearance process; external engineers need a sponsor and a one-week lead time for building passes. Onsite acceptance will need to be scheduled accordingly.

3) Fallback model: we would prefer a small distilled model that can run on a single-node for emergency processing. Is that supported with your runtime?

4) Security: we will require a signed SOC2 supplement and an on-site attestation checklist prior to any field engineer visit. Can you provide your standard text now so we can start procurement review?

Also — please confirm whether firmware and kernel-level updates pushed during maintenance will be staged via our jump host or require a physical media handoff. We will need a clear plan for out-of-band recovery if a rollback is required.

Thanks,
Li Cheng
Head of Infrastructure, NovaGenomics
[li.cheng@novagenomics.com]
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Li Cheng <li.cheng@novagenomics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Air-gapped fit assessment & scope confirmation

Hi Li — great, thanks for the specifics. Answers inline below and actions: 

1) Nightly windows & ad-hoc jobs: that profile matches the hardware options we attached. For your peak windows we recommend a 4-GPU node with mixed-precision quantization for the primary model and a 1-GPU reserve node sized for the distilled fallback. See the attached profile for throughput curves.

2) Onsite access & acceptance: understood on lead times. We will include acceptance test checklist that separates self-run tests (you can run) vs field-engineer tasks. We'll mark any task requiring physical presence so scheduling aligns with your clearance.

3) Distilled fallback: yes — our runtime supports a smaller quantized variant that can operate on a single 24GB GPU. We'll include an end-to-end runbook for failover and state sync.

4) SOC2 supplement & attestation: Priyom, can you attach the standard SOC2 supplement and the field-eng checklist?

5) Patch staging / rollback: our preferred pattern is staging artifacts on the jump host (signed packages). We provide signed binaries and a validated rollback image to be kept on-site. If network-limited, we can ship encrypted USB media under chain-of-custody. We'll document both options in the MOP.

Actions we own by 2026-08-05:
- Ben: procurement checklist + pricing for Private vs Dedicated options. [Ben: can you include lead times for hardware procurement and an SLA table.]
- Priyom: SOC2 supplement + field eng checklist + MOP draft updates.
- Hannah: acceptance test matrix and updated HW profile with estimated costs.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Li Cheng <li.cheng@novagenomics.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Air-gapped fit assessment & scope confirmation

Hi Li — looping in procurement details and a practical timeline.

Quick notes: 
- Procurement lead time: for standard 4x A40-class rack nodes (our recommended base), typical delivery to APAC sites ~10–12 weeks after PO. There is an accelerated channel (+2–3 weeks) at ~8% premium.
- Support & SLA: Private deployments come with an on-site support add-on (4hr on-call escalation for critical incidents) and optional annual HW refresh program. If you choose Dedicated instead, we can reserve capacity in our APAC pool with a 30-day provisioning SLA but it will not satisfy the airgap/regulatory control requirement.
- Commercials: attached is a redline PSA draft with our standard terms and an explicit clause for chain-of-custody media handling (contract-psa-redline.pdf).

Decision checklist for you to consider: 
1) If regulatory/airgap requirement is absolute -> Private on-prem (accepts longer procurement & field-eng timeline).
2) If you can accept logical isolation but not physical airgap -> Dedicated reserved capacity (faster time-to-live, lower ops for you).

Proposed timeline if Private is selected: PO + initial deposit -> 2–3 weeks (contract & SOC2 supplement sign) -> 10–12 weeks (hardware) -> 2 weeks (on-site install & acceptance).

If it helps, I can put together a side-by-side timeline + TCO spreadsheet.

Li — can you confirm whether procurement runs through your central vendor (we prefer a PO to Redwood) or you need Redwood to buy and invoice? That affects lead time.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions & Field Engineering, Redwood Inference
